description:
Make a cloned voice from recordings of one person speaking. THIS SPENDS MONEY: a one-off fee ($1.00 on the hosted service) is taken from credit, and it is not refunded when the voice is deleted. Confirm with the user before calling it. Set consent to true only after the user has told you, in this conversation, that the voice is their own or that the speaker has given permission to clone it and use it on calls; never assume it. The recordings go in as audio_urls: public https links the API downloads once and does not keep. This tool cannot upload files; for a file on disk, use the dashboard or the SDKs, or host it at a public link first. 30 seconds to a few minutes of one person speaking clearly, no music or other voices; mp3, wav, m4a, ogg, webm or flac, up to 10 MB each. elevenlabs takes 1 to 5 recordings; sarvam takes exactly 1 (10 to 30 seconds is enough) and needs language. An account holds at most 3 voices (account_limit_reached). There is no idempotency key: after a timeout, call list_voices before trying again, or the user may pay for two clones. To use the result, put its provider_voice_id in an agent's voice.tts.voice on one of its engines.

Requires scope `voices:write`.

audio_urls.description: Public https links to the recordings.

consent.description: Must be true, and only once the user has confirmed the voice is theirs or the speaker has given permission.

language.description: The language spoken in the recording, e.g. "ml-IN". Required for sarvam.

name.description: A name the user will recognise, e.g. "Dr. Meera, front desk".

provider.description: Where the clone is made, which decides the engines it speaks on: elevenlabs for the classic and deepgram_agent engines, sarvam for the sarvam engine (the one for Indian languages). Default elevenlabs. Gemini Live and OpenAI GPT-Live cannot use a cloned voice.

remove_background_noise.description: elevenlabs only. Cleans up a noisy recording; it can make a clean one worse.

name: create_voice_clone
title: Clone a voice
